definitions.gloss: handwriting with personal quirks; idiosyncratic penmanship
definitions.explanation: Handwriting whose individual style — slant, loops, oversized characters — makes it noticeably personal, often at the cost of legibility. Carries a slightly negative or apologetic nuance.

examples.japanese: {父|ちち}の{字|じ}は{癖字|くせじ}で{読|よ}みにくい。
examples.english: My father's handwriting is quirky and hard to read.

examples.japanese: {癖字|くせじ}なので{書類|しょるい}は{活字|かつじ}で{書|か}くようにしている。
examples.english: My handwriting is quirky, so I make sure to print on documents.

examples.japanese: {昔|むかし}の{手紙|てがみ}を{読|よ}み{返|かえ}したら、{祖母|そぼ}の{癖字|くせじ}が{懐|なつ}かしく{感|かん}じられた。
examples.english: Rereading old letters, I felt nostalgic for my grandmother's distinctive handwriting.

notes:
Compound of {癖|くせ} (habit; quirk) + {字|じ} (character; handwriting). The {癖|くせ} element gives it a mildly negative tone — usually about legibility, sometimes affectionate when describing a familiar person.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {癖字|くせじ}で{書|か}く: to write in quirky handwriting
- ひどい{癖字|くせじ}: terrible/illegible handwriting
- {癖字|くせじ}を{直|なお}す: to correct one's handwriting quirks

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {悪筆|あくひつ}: bad handwriting — straightforwardly negative, focuses on poor quality
- {達筆|たっぴつ}: skilled, flowing calligraphy — positive, often hard to read for the opposite reason
- {下手|へた}な{字|じ}: clumsy handwriting — emphasizes lack of skill, not personality
